review.source: Actual written N1904 and original Berean publisher rows, reviewed against displayed BSB; distinct peer pending.

12:1.sourceText: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἐπορεύθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς σάββασιν διὰ τῶν σπορίμων· οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπείνασαν καὶ ἤρξαντο τίλλειν στάχυας καὶ ἐσθίειν.
12:1.targetText: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began to pick the heads of grain and eat them.

groups.note: Actual temporal dative Sabbath supplies the English preposition.
The repeated English object refers to the same written heads of grain shared by picking and eating.

unmappedSource.reason: English starts the second sentence without an overt local connective.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:2.sourceText: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἰδόντες εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἰδοὺ οἱ μαθηταί σου ποιοῦσιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ποιεῖν ἐν σαββάτῳ.
12:2.targetText: When the Pharisees saw this, they said to Him, “Look, Your disciples are doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath.”

groups.note: Actual circumstantial seeing participle supplies the English temporal clause.
Actual not plus be-permitted supplies the English negative predicate.

studyHeads.note: Actual permission predicate is the lexical head under the separate written negative.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the introductory connective and second doing infinitive implicit.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for the actual seeing participle, without a separate source demonstrative.

12:3.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυεὶδ ὅτε ἐπείνασεν καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ;
12:3.targetText: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

groups.note: English explicitly names the subject marked by the actual pronominal article. The source anchor is the written article, not a Greek name.
Actual second-plural reading supplies the English inquiry auxiliary and verb, distinct from the written negative.
Actual first named actor shares the hungry predicate with the companions in English plural agreement.
Actual those with him supplies the English companion phrase.

studyHeads.note: Actual genitive person supplies the association.
Actual pronominal article supplies the people in the with-him construction.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the discourse connective and the written dative speech recipients.

12:4.sourceText: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγον, ὃ οὐκ ἐξὸν ἦν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν οὐδὲ τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, εἰ μὴ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν μόνοις;
12:4.targetText: He entered the house of God, and he and his companions ate the consecrated bread, which was not lawful for them to eat, but only for the priests.

groups.note: Actual entering verb with its directed-into preposition is compressed into English entered.

studyHeads.note: Actual entering verb supplies the head and its directional preposition remains anchored.

groups.note: Actual presentation designation when joined to bread supplies the contextual English modifier.
Actual not for him nor for those with him is collapsed into the English plural group.

studyHeads.note: Actual dative him is the first participant. The companion construction is also present in the group.

groups.note: Actual except formula rendered by the adversative.
Actual dative priest noun supplies the prepositional recipient relation.

unmappedSource.reason: English opens the report without the actual how marker.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English specifies the actors of the plural eating verb from the preceding context. No actor noun or pronoun is printed with eating here.

12:5.sourceText: ἢ οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὅτι τοῖς σάββασιν οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τὸ σάββατον βεβηλοῦσιν καὶ ἀναίτιοί εἰσιν;
12:5.targetText: Or haven’t you read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and yet are innocent?

groups.note: Actual negator and reading predicate supply English contraction and attached inquiry.

studyHeads.note: Actual not supplies the negative in the contraction.
Actual reading supplies the lexical predicate.

groups.note: Actual temporal dative Sabbath supplies the temporal relation; the later Sabbath remains independent.

12:6.sourceText: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι τοῦ ἱεροῦ μεῖζόν ἐστιν ὧδε.
12:6.targetText: But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.

groups.note: Actual comparative genitive temple supplies the English comparison relation.
Actual neuter comparative adjective functions substantivally. The publisher says One greater; installed BSB says something greater.

12:7.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ἐγνώκειτε τί ἐστιν Ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν, οὐκ ἂν κατεδικάσατε τοὺς ἀναιτίους.
12:7.targetText: If only you had known the meaning of ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the innocent.

groups.note: Actual what-it-is question is recast as the English meaning expression.

studyHeads.note: Actual interrogative participates in the question about the saying’s force.

groups.note: Actual counterfactual particle supplies the English modal relation.
Actual second-plural condemnation supplies the English subject and predicate under separate modal and negator.

unmappedSource.reason: English uses the conditioned construction and list punctuation without separately rendering the opening contrast or the conjunction in the quote.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the counterfactual condition emphatic; no corresponding independent exclusive word is written.

12:8.sourceText: κύριος γάρ ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
12:8.targetText: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

12:9.sourceText: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτῶν.
12:9.targetText: Moving on from there, Jesus entered their synagogue,

groups.note: Actual came into becomes a transitive English motion predicate.

studyHeads.note: Actual coming verb supplies the motion predicate with its directional preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: English opens with a temporal participle and no separate coordinator.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the contextual subject; actual N1904 prints no local name.

12:10.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος χεῖρα ἔχων ξηράν· καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Εἰ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεῦσαι; ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.
12:10.targetText: and a man with a withered hand was there. In order to accuse Jesus, they asked Him, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”

groups.note: Actual polar question marker and permission predicate supply this English question.

studyHeads.note: Actual permission predicate supplies the lexical head.

groups.note: Actual temporal dative Sabbath supplies the English prepositional relation.
English names the referent of the actual genitive pronoun used with accusing. Preserve the written pronoun, distinct from Him with asking.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the attention marker, continuation conjunction and speech-introducing participle.

unmappedTarget.reason: English opens the scene with an existential clause. No written finite be verb occurs.

12:11.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τίς ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν ἄνθρωπος ὃς ἕξει πρόβατον ἕν, καὶ ἐὰν ἐμπέσῃ τοῦτο τοῖς σάββασιν εἰς βόθυνον, οὐχὶ κρατήσει αὐτὸ καὶ ἐγερεῖ;
12:11.targetText: He replied, “If one of you has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will he not take hold of it and lift it out?

groups.note: Actual interrogative and person noun introduce the same person within an English conditional question.

studyHeads.note: Actual person noun supplies the nominal head.

groups.note: Actual temporal dative supplies the English relation.
Actual grasping predicate supplies the English question subject, auxiliary and action.
Actual object is shared by grasping and the coordinated lifting. English repeats it.
Actual raising predicate supplies this English split verb.

unmappedSource.reason: English recasts the introductory connective, reply recipients, finite question frame and possessive relative as one conditional question.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:12.sourceText: πόσῳ οὖν διαφέρει ἄνθρωπος προβάτου. ὥστε ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν καλῶς ποιεῖν.
12:12.targetText: How much more valuable is a man than a sheep! Therefore it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”

groups.note: Actual temporal dative Sabbath supplies the English relation.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual inferential connector is implicit in the English exclamation.

12:13.sourceText: τότε λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα. καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ὑγιὴς ὡς ἡ ἄλλη.
12:13.targetText: Then Jesus said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored to full use, just like the other.

groups.note: Actual dative man supplies the speech addressee and its English relation.
Both English it words resume the explicitly named local hand, once as the patient of stretching and once under restoration.
Actual stretching supplies the second English split verb and explicit subject.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the contextual speaker. No written name corresponds here.

12:14.sourceText: ἐξελθόντες δὲ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι συμβούλιον ἔλαβον κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.
12:14.targetText: But the Pharisees went out and plotted how they might kill Jesus.

groups.note: Actual took counsel supplies the English plotting predicate.

studyHeads.note: Actual counsel noun contributes the planning meaning.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual against him is implicit in the following explicit plot to kill him.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes going out a coordinated finite action where actual going out is participial.

12:15.sourceText: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς γνοὺς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν. καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πολλοί, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτοὺς πάντας,
12:15.targetText: Aware of this, Jesus withdrew from that place. Large crowds followed Him, and He healed them all,

groups.note: Actual knowing participle supplies the awareness construction.

unmappedSource.reason: The English sentence boundaries leave the two actual introductory connectives implicit.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for the awareness; no actual demonstrative is printed with this verb.
The publisher prints a crowd noun in this clause. Actual N1904 has only the substantive many.

12:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ φανερὸν αὐτὸν ποιήσωσιν·
12:16.targetText: warning them not to make Him known.

groups.note: Actual clause marker supplies the English complement relationship.

unmappedSource.reason: English gives the warning as a dependent participle without a separate opening conjunction.

12:17.sourceText: ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος
12:17.targetText: This was to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:

groups.note: Actual purpose conjunction supplies the English fulfilment relation.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual saying participle is implicit at the English quote boundary.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula in the recast purpose clause.

12:18.sourceText: Ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς μου ὃν ᾑρέτισα, ὁ ἀγαπητός μου ὃν εὐδόκησεν ἡ ψυχή μου· θήσω τὸ Πνεῦμά μου ἐπ’ αὐτόν, καὶ κρίσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπαγγελεῖ.
12:18.targetText: “Here is My Servant, whom I have chosen, My beloved, in whom My soul delights. I will put My Spirit on Him, and He will proclaim justice to the nations.

groups.note: Actual dative nations supplies the recipient relation.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The publisher Greek explicitly prints a preposition preceding whom here. Actual N1904 has the relative without that preposition.

12:19.sourceText: οὐκ ἐρίσει οὐδὲ κραυγάσει, οὐδὲ ἀκούσει τις ἐν ταῖς πλατείαις τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ.
12:19.targetText: He will not quarrel or cry out; no one will hear His voice in the streets.

groups.note: Actual future quarrelling is distinct from its direct written negative.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:20.sourceText: κάλαμον συντετριμμένον οὐ κατεάξει καὶ λίνον τυφόμενον οὐ σβέσει, ἕως ἂν ἐκβάλῃ εἰς νῖκος τὴν κρίσιν.
12:20.targetText: A bruised reed He will not break, and a smoldering wick He will not extinguish, till He leads justice to victory.

groups.note: The first actual future action retains its independent negative.
The second actual future action retains its independent negative.
Actual temporal conjunction with modal particle supplies the final boundary.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:21.sourceText: καὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ ἔθνη ἐλπιοῦσιν.
12:21.targetText: In His name the nations will put their hope.”

groups.note: Actual dative name supplies the relation; the article does not supply an independent preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The English starts this clause without a separate and.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:22.sourceText: Τότε προσηνέχθη αὐτῷ δαιμονιζόμενος τυφλὸς καὶ κωφός· καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτόν, ὥστε τὸν κωφὸν λαλεῖν καὶ βλέπειν.
12:22.targetText: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to Jesus, and He healed the man so that he could speak and see.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English expands the actual adjective into a finite relative. No local copula is written.

12:23.sourceText: καὶ ἐξίσταντο πάντες οἱ ὄχλοι καὶ ἔλεγον Μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς Δαυείδ;
12:23.targetText: The crowds were astounded and asked, “Could this be the Son of David?”

groups.note: Actual negative-expectation question particle and copular proposition are recast as an English modal question.

studyHeads.note: Actual question marker supplies the marked inquiry.
Actual copula supplies the predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the introductory coordinator and quantifier all implicit.

12:24.sourceText: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες εἶπον Οὗτος οὐκ ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια εἰ μὴ ἐν τῷ Βεελζεβοὺλ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων.
12:24.targetText: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “Only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, does this man drive out demons.”

groups.note: Actual circumstantial hearing participle supplies the English temporal clause.
Actual demonstrative pronoun identifies the person named more explicitly by the English phrase.
Actual not with an except formula is recast as English Only.

studyHeads.note: Actual exception conjunction heads the full construction.

groups.note: Actual expelling verb supplies the auxiliary as well as the English verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English gives the hearing clause an object. Its actual participle has no printed object.

12:25.sourceText: εἰδὼς δὲ τὰς ἐνθυμήσεις αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πᾶσα βασιλεία μερισθεῖσα καθ’ ἑαυτῆς ἐρημοῦται, καὶ πᾶσα πόλις ἢ οἰκία μερισθεῖσα καθ’ ἑαυτῆς οὐ σταθήσεται.
12:25.targetText: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and every city or household divided against itself will not stand.

groups.note: Actual standing predicate supplies the English future, apart from its written negative.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the discourse connective implicit at the new sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The contextual speaker is named in English without a parallel actual name.

12:26.sourceText: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς τὸν Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλει, ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν ἐμερίσθη· πῶς οὖν σταθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ;
12:26.targetText: If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then can his kingdom stand?

groups.note: Actual future standing is expressed as an English modal question.

unmappedSource.reason: English opens the conditional without a separate and.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:27.sourceText: καὶ εἰ ἐγὼ ἐν Βεελζεβοὺλ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν ἐν τίνι ἐκβάλλουσιν; διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ κριταὶ ἔσονται ὑμῶν.
12:27.targetText: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.

groups.note: English repeats the explicit demon object in the second expelling clause, where Greek leaves the object implicit.
The actual second expelling predicate supplies the English inquiry auxiliary and verb.
Actual for-this construction supplies the inference.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:28.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ἐν Πνεύματι Θεοῦ ἐγὼ ἐκβάλλω τὰ δαιμόνια, ἄρα ἔφθασεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ.
12:28.targetText: But if I drive out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:29.sourceText: ἢ πῶς δύναταί τις εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἁρπάσαι, ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον δήσῃ τὸν ἰσχυρόν, καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει;
12:29.targetText: Or again, how can anyone enter a strong man’s house and steal his possessions, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can plunder his house.

groups.note: Actual enter and its following into are compressed into English enter.

studyHeads.note: Actual entering infinitive supplies the head with its direction preserved.

groups.note: Actual if not supplies the exception condition.
Actual binding predicate provides both the understood subject and the lexical action.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the introductory conjunction of the consequence unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English expands the alternative-introducing connective with an explicit repetition adverb.

12:30.sourceText: ὁ μὴ ὢν μετ’ ἐμοῦ κατ’ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν, καὶ ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ’ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει.
12:30.targetText: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.

groups.note: Actual gathering participle is recast as a finite English relative predicate.

12:31.sourceText: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πᾶσα ἁμαρτία καὶ βλασφημία ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, ἡ δὲ τοῦ Πνεύματος βλασφημία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.
12:31.targetText: Therefore I tell you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

groups.note: Actual for-this construction supplies the inference.
Actual genitive Spirit states the target of the blasphemy, expressed through an English preposition.
The second actual forgiveness predicate supplies both English verb components under its local negative.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:32.sourceText: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν εἴπῃ λόγον κατὰ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ κατὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος τοῦ Ἁγίου, οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ οὔτε ἐν τούτῳ τῷ αἰῶνι οὔτε ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι.
12:32.targetText: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come.

groups.note: Actual first indefinite relative construction.
Actual second indefinite relative construction.
The second actual forgiveness predicate supplies the English future under its separately printed negator.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the opening connector and recasts the two written dative recipients as the passive subjects.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:33.sourceText: Ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον καλὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ καλόν, ἢ ποιήσατε τὸ δένδρον σαπρὸν καὶ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ σαπρόν· ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ καρποῦ τὸ δένδρον γινώσκεται.
12:33.targetText: Make a tree good and its fruit will be good, or make a tree bad and its fruit will be bad; for a tree is known by its fruit.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening alternative marker is implicit; the second marker remains mapped to or.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The actual first imperative also governs the fruit adjective. English uses a supplied prediction instead.
The actual second imperative also governs the fruit adjective. English uses a supplied prediction instead.
The English specifies whose fruit in the proverb. The Greek prints a definite article without a local possessor pronoun.

12:34.sourceText: γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς δύνασθε ἀγαθὰ λαλεῖν πονηροὶ ὄντες; ἐκ γὰρ τοῦ περισσεύματος τῆς καρδίας τὸ στόμα λαλεῖ.
12:34.targetText: You brood of vipers, how can you who are evil say anything good? For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes the people being addressed explicit in a vocative without a written pronoun.

12:35.sourceText: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει ἀγαθά, καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ θησαυροῦ ἐκβάλλει πονηρά.
12:35.targetText: The good man brings good things out of his good store of treasure, and the evil man brings evil things out of his evil store of treasure.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English provides the possessor of the good store from the subject. There is no local written possessor.
English supplies the possessor of the evil store in the parallel clause. There is no local written possessor.

12:36.sourceText: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως·
12:36.targetText: But I tell you that men will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they have spoken.

groups.note: Actual subordination of the speech supplies the English conjunction.
Actual future active speaking is rendered as an English perfect, viewing the words as already spoken at the accounting.
Actual concerning preposition governs a resumptive pronoun referring to every word. English integrates it into for every ... word.

unmappedSource.reason: English omits the object relative before the speaking clause and the actual resumptive pronoun after concerning.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:37.sourceText: ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.
12:37.targetText: For by your words you will be acquitted, and by your words you will be condemned.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:38.sourceText: Τότε ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ τινες τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε, θέλομεν ἀπὸ σοῦ σημεῖον ἰδεῖν.
12:38.targetText: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees said to Him, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from You.”

groups.note: Actual replying and speech-introducing saying are rendered as one English speech predicate.

studyHeads.note: Actual saying supplies the lexical head, with answering retained as part of the source construction.

groups.note: Actual dative pronoun supplies the utterance recipient, independent of the replying predicate.

12:39.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλὶς σημεῖον ἐπιζητεῖ, καὶ σημεῖον οὐ δοθήσεται αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ τὸ σημεῖον Ἰωνᾶ τοῦ προφήτου.
12:39.targetText: Jesus replied, “A wicked and adulterous generation demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.

groups.note: English names the person supplied by the written pronominal article. The Greek source remains the article.
Actual answering participle and saying verb are combined as one English replying predicate.

studyHeads.note: Actual answering supplies the reply sense.

groups.note: Actual no sign is shortened to English none, with both written source words retained.

studyHeads.note: Actual negative supplies the initial head.

unmappedSource.reason: English leaves the introductory connector and actual dative recipients unexpressed.

12:40.sourceText: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἦν Ἰωνᾶς ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ τοῦ κήτους τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ τῆς γῆς τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας.
12:40.targetText: For as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:41.sourceText: ἄνδρες Νινευεῖται ἀναστήσονται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτήν· ὅτι μετενόησαν εἰς τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰωνᾶ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε.
12:41.targetText: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.

12:42.sourceText: βασίλισσα νότου ἐγερθήσεται ἐν τῇ κρίσει μετὰ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης καὶ κατακρινεῖ αὐτήν· ὅτι ἦλθεν ἐκ τῶν περάτων τῆς γῆς ἀκοῦσαι τὴν σοφίαν Σολομῶνος, καὶ ἰδοὺ πλεῖον Σολομῶνος ὧδε.
12:42.targetText: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.

groups.note: Actual substantivized neuter comparative supplies the English comparison subject.

12:43.sourceText: Ὅταν δὲ τὸ ἀκάθαρτον πνεῦμα ἐξέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, διέρχεται δι’ ἀνύδρων τόπων ζητοῦν ἀνάπαυσιν, καὶ οὐχ εὑρίσκει.
12:43.targetText: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it.

groups.note: English repeats the explicitly named local object as a pronoun after find.

12:44.sourceText: τότε λέγει Εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου ἐπιστρέψω ὅθεν ἐξῆλθον· καὶ ἐλθὸν εὑρίσκει σχολάζοντα καὶ σεσαρωμένον καὶ κεκοσμημένον.
12:44.targetText: Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’ On its return, it finds the house vacant, swept clean, and put in order.

12:45.targetText: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there; and the final plight of that man is worse than the first. So will it be with this wicked generation.”
